The appellant has filed this appeal against the award passed in M.C.O.P.No.948 of 2016, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (In the Court of Small Causes Court), Chennai, dated The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs S.Usharani on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41511678/

sentences.text:
When the matter was taken up, the learned counsel for the appellant submitted that, in C.M.A.
No.3597 of 2021 filed by the insurance company, the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the van.

However, the Tribunal erroneously applied the principle of composite negligence and fixed the entire liability upon the owner of the two-wheeler, who is insured with the appellant/insurance company, on the ground that the van allegedly did not have a valid insurance policy.

It was further submitted that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the two-wheeler, and therefore, fixing the entire liability upon the driver of the two-wheeler is illegal and liable to be set aside.
To support his arguments, he relied upon the rough sketch (Ex.R2 series) marked on his side.

By pointing out the rough 3 of 10 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 26/08/2025 07:59:12 pm ) sketch, the learned counsel submitted that the accident happened in the middle of the road and that there was a median.
Therefore, there was no possibility of turning right to reach the petrol bunk as claimed by the claimant.
Between the petrol bunk and the place of occurrence, there was a median for about one kilometre.
Hence, the defence put forth by the claimant is not acceptable.
He therefore prayed that the findings of the Tribunal be set aside.

3. By way of reply, the learned counsel for the respondents submitted that, at the time of the accident, the driver of the two-wheeler attempted to turn right, and in doing so, the van, which was following, dashed against him.
As a result, the two-wheeler was damaged on the right side.
In support of this, he relied on the Motor Vehicle Inspection Report (Ex.R2 series).
On considering the said report, the Tribunal also noted that the damages to the two-wheeler were on the right-hand side.

4. Admittedly, as per the rough sketch, and as rightly pointed out by the appellants counsel, the petrol bunk was on the right side of the place of occurrence and there was a median in between,
making it impossible to 4 of 10 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 26/08/2025 07:59:12 pm ) reach the petrol bunk from that point.
However, the rough sketch also clearly reveals that the rider of the two-wheeler attempted to turn right.
Due to this manoeuvre, the two-wheeler was hit on the right side, causing fatal injuries to the pillion rider, who later succumbed to those injuries.
Therefore, the negligence on the part of the rider of the two-wheeler was proved by the claimant.
5. However, while fixing the compensation, the Tribunal noted that there was no insurance policy for either the two-wheeler or the van.
The van driver drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two-wheeler from behind.
Since the van was not covered by a valid insurance policy, the Tribunal fixed the entire liability upon the insurance company of the two-wheeler.
Considering the manner of the accident, this Court holds that 70% contributory negligence is attributable to the rider of the two-wheeler and 30% to the driver of the van.
Accordingly, the findings of the Tribunal are modified.
6. The appellant is liable to pay only 70% of the compensation.
The claimant has also filed a cross-objection for enhancement.

The learned 5 of 10 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 26/08/2025 07:59:12 pm ) counsel for the claimant submitted that the loss of consortium as The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs S.Usharani on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41511678/
3 well as the income of the deceased were not properly appreciated by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: The income of the deceased was proved to be Rs.12,000/- per month by examining the Manager of the concern where the deceased was employed, but the same was not properly considered.

7. The learned Judge of the Tribunal, despite noting that the deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month, fixed the income at only Rs.10,000/- without assigning any reason, which warrants interference.
Therefore, the income of the deceased is fixed at Rs.12,000/- per month.
Loss of consortium is fixed at Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 3 = Rs.1,20,000).
The other heads of compensation awarded by the Tribunal are confirmed.

8. Calculation Notional Income = Rs.12,000/-
25% Future Prospects = 12,000 + 3,000 = 15,000/- After 1/3 deduction = 15,000  5,000=
Rs.10,000/- Loss of dependency = Rs.10,000 x 12 x 14 = Rs.16,80,000/-

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.14,70,000/- to Rs.18,30,000/-, which shall carry interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.
